transcript: Last night my friend Joel and I went to see the light in the Piazza at City Center and it was amazing. This is a revival, and the basic premise is that while a mother and daughter, Margaret and Clara, are on a trip to Italy, Clara falls head over heels for one of the local men. Margaret has reservations about it, given that Clara suffered an accident as a child that impacted her mental development. The story is relatively simple, and the star of the show is the score, which is uniquely lush and subtle, but still grand and emotive. This was a gorgeously performed production by the entire cast and orchestra, in particular Ruthie N. Miles and Anna Zavelson, whose star as Margaret and Clara gave jaw droppingly good performances. Anna tone is bright and youthful, but not at all shrill or thin, and ruthie's voice and acting are precise and heartbreaking. Last night was actually the closing performance, but feel free to take this as a general recommendation for anything that they're in in the future. Ruthie and miles is currently in Sweeney Todd, so go check that out with that another playbill for my collection.
